facts.search_today: Full-text grep over every markdown/text file: 5.1 s with a cold disk cache, 0.05 s warm, on a 4-core cloud VM. git status 0.02 s. Looking a term up in manifest.jsonl 0.004 s.
facts.search_at_40k: Projected by linear scaling (x8.9) to 40,000 files: grep about 45 s cold and 0.4 s warm on the VM, slower on the phone; about 1.2 GB tracked and 3 GB of git history.
facts.manifest_coverage: manifest.jsonl lists 585 of the 4,509 files today, so it is not kept current.
facts.jev_per_request: Each Jev triage request carries one section of at most 8,000 characters (about 1,900 input tokens) against a 32,000-token per-question limit, so request size does not grow with the vault. Triage cost grows linearly: 6.4 million tokens for 3,415 sections today.
facts.jev_speed: Jev answers in a median 0.16 s per request and requests run in parallel.
facts.scope: Keeping the corpus itself current is the wiki-admin agent package's job, a separate layer; these questions are about retrieval and about each turn's writes to the memory layers.
facts.write_order: After each turn the memory layers are written one after another, not concurrently: static memory (vault files and their manifest/labels), the graph layer (code-review-graph tree-sitter AST and Graphify), and episodic memory (RESUME.md plus its own SQLite database).

options.custom_harness: The operator's planned system. Third-party stacks are broken into assets and only the useful parts are folded in. Claude Code is the harness, customised with hooks, skills, subagents and mods. Routing is a UserPromptSubmit hook that asks Jev typed questions and sends unsure cases to a Sonnet or Opus subagent. Episodic memory is a Stop hook where Jev decides what to keep and writes it to RESUME.md and its own SQLite database; the same hook then updates the static layer and the code-review-graph AST in sequence. Semantic retrieval uses the vault, its manifest and per-section Jev labels, with grep and Jev relevance ranking. Graphify and code-review-graph stay as the graph layers. Everything is files in git; no extra database servers. Much of it is not built yet.
options.third_party_servers: Run the third-party servers whole, as their projects ship them: OmniRoute as a localhost gateway that every prompt passes through, with its own SQLite store; mem0 for episodic memory with Postgres and Neo4j; OB1 / Terrestrial Brain on Supabase or Postgres with pgvector and LLM-based schema routing; plus Graphify and code-review-graph. Runs in Docker Compose on the GCP VM, reached from the phone over Tailscale. The operator earlier found OB1 intrusive and said it attempts to hijack prompts.
options.baseline_claude_code: Plain Claude Code with no additions: it reads AGENTS.md and the files it is pointed at, uses its built-in memory files and subagents, and searches the vault with grep when asked. No Jev, no routing layer, no memory servers, no graph tools.
